content_units: Ontario Rent Increase Checklist for This Situation
Your goal is to build a clean paper trail, confirm what is being changed, and avoid agreeing to anything unclear in writing.
For the facts you gave, the key practical issue is documenting the proposed   rent increase   and the proposed   new parking charge   separately.
What to Gather and Track
Item   What to document   Why it matters   Status for your scenario
Lease start date   Signed lease showing   2024-07-01   start date   Helps track timing and whether 12 months have passed   Keep copy ready
Current lawful rent   Proof current rent is   CAD 1,850     Baseline for any increase   Save latest rent receipts/bank records
Parking terms   Lease/addendum/emails showing parking was   included     Confirms whether parking was part of the original deal   Highlight exact wording
Landlord notice email   Save the   2025-05-10   email in full with headers/screenshots/PDF   Preserves exact wording and proposed dates/amounts   Archive it now
Proposed new amounts   Rent to   CAD 1,940   and parking   CAD 125/month   starting   2025-06-01     Separates the two charges for review   Write them in your timeline
Notice format   Whether landlord provided the official written notice form for rent increase   Important administrative detail to track   Note if only email was sent
Timing timeline   Date sent:   2025-05-10  ; proposed start:   2025-06-01     Timing is a core item to verify   Keep as a simple dated log
Payment history   E-transfers, bank statements, receipts, ledger   Shows what you have actually been paying   Save monthly proof
Questions and Documents to Request from the Landlord
Use short, neutral written requests. Ask for each item separately so the record stays clear.
Option 1:   Written rent-change breakdown     Ask them to state the current rent, new rent, effective date, and legal notice used   Keeps the rent issue separate from parking
Request breakdown

Option 2:   Parking change explanation     Ask whether parking is being removed from the tenancy and recharged as a separate service, and on what basis   Clarifies whether this is a lease change versus a new optional service
Review rules
Option 3:   Copy of any official notice served     Request a PDF/photo of the completed notice form, if one exists, and the date it was served   Helps you track notice method and dates
Find forms

Option 4:   Updated rent ledger or amendment draft     Ask for a written document showing exactly what total monthly payment they expect starting 2025-06-01   Prevents later disputes about what you agreed to
Tenant guide
Practical Tenant Checklist to Follow
- Save the original lease, parking addendum, and any ad/listing that mentioned included parking.
- Export the landlord’s 2025-05-10 email as PDF and keep screenshots.
- Make a one-page timeline with:
- Lease start:   2024-07-01
- Email received:   2025-05-10
- Proposed change date:   2025-06-01
- Current rent:   CAD 1,850
- Proposed rent:   CAD 1,940
- Proposed parking fee:   CAD 125
- Check whether parking is described in the lease as:
- included in rent
- a separate service
- assigned spot/garage right
- optional amenity
- Ask the landlord, in writing, for:
- the exact new lawful rent they say applies
- the exact parking arrangement they say applies
- the form/notice used
- the date they say notice was served
- whether they want one payment or separate payments
- Keep communications in writing only if possible.
- Do not rely on phone calls; if one happens, send a same-day recap email.
- Keep proof of every payment made after the proposal.
- If you disagree, avoid vague replies like “okay” or “sounds fine”; respond with a neutral request for clarification and documents.
- If parking is important, ask whether your spot remains reserved while the issue is being clarified.
Ready-to-Send Message Template
Subject: Request for written details of proposed rent and parking changes
Hello [Landlord Name],
I am writing about your email of May 10, 2025 regarding a proposed rent increase from CAD 1,850 to CAD 1,940 and a new parking charge of CAD 125 per month effective June 1, 2025.
For my records, please send:
- the written notice/form for the proposed rent increase
- the date the notice was served
- confirmation of the current lawful rent and the proposed new rent
- confirmation of how parking is being treated, since parking was previously included
- any updated lease addendum or written breakdown showing the total monthly amount you are requesting as of June 1, 2025
Please reply by email so I can keep complete records.
Thank you,
[Your Name]
[Unit Address]
